study: Order-flow pilot: when the 60 seconds before a desk-style pre-square entry show buyers lifting the ask (trade-side flow) or a bid-heavy top of book, does the next 3 minutes pay more than other pre-square entries, after crossing the spread?
origin: Operator 10/21, after the confirmation-indicator FAIL: what predicts a 3-minute run? Bar indicators have none. Order flow is the classic 1-5 minute source and is untested here on the trade side. Book imbalance was tested 10/4 (depth_book_prereg.json: Nasdaq OBI on 7,353 gapper entries, 120 s): gated minus rest -3.3 / -0.6 bp, UNDERPOWERED, no verdict.
prior: LOW. Public order flow on 1-minute-delayed-decision retail execution is crowded; the 10/4 book-imbalance read leaned the wrong way.
data: Alpaca historical SIP trades and NBBO quotes (free once 15 minutes old; data-only account in secrets_data.json). Entries: ALL PRE onsets from the indicator_confirm_hist pipeline (~92k: warehouse 2026-05-11 .. 10-15, 400-name sample, warm %R; the 80% IEX bar-coverage rule does NOT apply, since the features are tick-based), decision minute m = onset + 1, 10:00-15:27 so the 3-minute exit is inside RTH. Sample: 16,000 entries (8,000 per half), drawn by seed sha256('order-flow-pilot') before any tick is fetched. No spend.
timing: T = the start of decision minute m (ET), i.e. the moment the onset bar is complete. Features read SIP trades in [T - 60 s, T) and the NBBO at T. Entry: the ask of the last NBBO quote at or before T + 1 s. Exits: the bid of the last NBBO quote at or before T + 1 s + H. No quote within 5 s before the read time -> the entry is dropped (counted).

features.OFI60: trade-side flow over [T - 60 s, T): each trade signed by Lee-Ready against the NBBO mid prevailing at the trade (above mid +1, below -1, at mid by the tick test vs the previous trade price, unchanged -> previous sign); OFI60 = signed share volume / total share volume. Trades with conditions that are not regular-way (odd-lot inclusive; exclude out-of-sequence, average-price, derivatively priced, prior-reference and extended-hours conditions) are dropped before signing. Fewer than 5 trades in the window -> OFI60 missing (entry leaves G1 and G3).
features.QI: top-of-book size imbalance at T: (bid_size - ask_size) / (bid_size + ask_size) of the last NBBO at or before T.
features.MICRO: information only: (microprice - mid) / mid at T, microprice = (bid x ask_size + ask x bid_size) / (bid_size + ask_size).

hypotheses.G1_trade_flow: IN = PRE entries with OFI60 in the top tercile; OUT = the rest with OFI60.
hypotheses.G2_book: IN = QI in the top tercile; OUT = the rest.
hypotheses.G3_both: IN = OFI60 AND QI both in their top terciles; OUT = the rest with both.

cuts: tercile cut points computed on half A only (outcome-blind: features only) and applied to both halves; written to the count file before any outcome is fetched.
outcome: PRIMARY H = 180 s. gross = mid(T + 1 s + H) / mid(T + 1 s) - 1; net = bid(T + 1 s + H) / ask(T + 1 s) - 1 (the whole spread inside). Information: H = 60, 120, 300 s.
statistic: gated minus rest per day on GROSS (IN mean - OUT mean, days with >= 3 entries each side), day-equal, day-clustered t (df = days - 1). Within-sample comparison: every entry is a PRE entry at the same kind of moment, so the rest is the control (as depth_book). Information: the same split within each hour of the day.
multiplicity: 3 tests: one-sided p 0.025 / 3 at df = days - 1.
power: 16,000 entries registered now (the earlier 'raise to 16,000 if MDE > 7 bp' rule always fired on the depth-study scaling, which does not transfer: gappers with 15 bp spreads scored on net). OUTCOME-BLIND projection after the features are fetched: for each hypothesis and half, the day-clustered SE of (IN - OUT) per-day means of the 3-minute SIP BAR returns at each entry's same-name control minute (decision minute drawn as indicator_confirm_hist, seed tag 'order-flow-ctrl'; bars from the warehouse, no tick outcome read), projected MDE = (t_crit + 0.84) x that SE, judged against 5 bp. Printed with the count step; it does not change the sample.
pass: per hypothesis, in BOTH halves: gated minus rest on gross >= +5 bp with t >= t_crit; gated mean NET > 0 (it pays after crossing the spread); name-day-equal difference > 0; drop-3-names and drop-3-days >= 0. FAIL: t <= -2 in a half, or the 97.5% upper bound below +5 bp in both halves. Otherwise UNDERPOWERED. Floors: 1,000 IN entries and 20 days per half (G3: 300), else UNDERPOWERED.
if_pass: a pilot pass is a hypothesis, not an edge. (1) Confirm on 60 earlier sessions with the same fetch rule and the same bar. (2) The live-feed bar: the same hypothesis with IEX trades signed against IEX quotes (Alpaca feed=iex historical) on the same entries: gated minus rest gross >= 0 with one-sided t >= 1.64 pooled over both halves, on >= 1,000 IN entries with >= 5 IEX trades in the window; if it fails, the SIP result cannot be traded on the free feed and no live work follows. Only after both: a result-skeptic review and a forward paper test.
if_fail: trade-side flow and top-of-book imbalance before a pre-square entry are closed at 3 minutes for effects >= 5 bp on SIP; together with depth_book (10/4) order flow is not the free-feed route to a 3-minute edge.
information_only: IEX-only trade signing (the live-feed version of OFI60)
share of entries whose 3-minute max favourable excursion clears 2x the spread, by group
terciles cut within each hour of the day (time-of-day confound)
OFI60 effect within terciles of the onset bar's own return (the onset-bar-size confound)
no_retuning: 60 s window, Lee-Ready signing, the trade-condition filter, terciles on half A, 180 s, the 5 bp bar, the sample size rule and the seed are fixed.
declared_deviations: SIP trades are consolidated and timestamped by the SIP, not by the venue; signing against the SIP NBBO is approximate (Lee-Ready error ~10-15% in the literature)
historical SIP is not what the live desk sees (IEX); the live question is a separate step in if_pass
the decision is at the minute boundary; live acts intrabar
script: tools/studies/order_flow_pilot.py (to be written; reuses indicator_confirm_hist for PRE entries and exec_report / momentum_alert_ticks helpers for SIP trades and quotes). Steps: --sample (draw entries), --fetch-features (trades + T quote), count step (cuts, MDE), --fetch-outcomes, --score after a result-skeptic READY.
fetch_plan: Requests per entry: trades [T - 60 s, T) (1, more if paged), NBBO [T - 5 s, T + 1 s] (1), NBBO [t - 5 s, t] at t = T + 1 s + 60 / 120 / 180 / 300 s (4): ~6-7 per entry, ~100k for 16,000 entries, ~11-12 hours at <= 150 requests/min. Fetch at any time (amended_2), paced, into a per-entry cache with resume. Order: (1) pre-step, (2) features (trades + the T quote) for all entries, (3) count step, (4) outcome quotes. Abort the run if > 2% of entries fail after retries.
pre_step: Before any feature is computed: fetch 20 seeded entries' trades and quotes and print, per tape (A/B = CTA, C = UTP), the observed trade condition codes with counts and whether size, conditions, tape, bid_size and ask_size are populated. The exact keep/drop condition list per tape is then registered as an amendment, from the CTA and UTP specifications and this inventory (no feature or outcome is computed before it). Drop rule by intent: drop extended-hours, sold-out-of-sequence, average-price, derivatively-priced, prior-reference-price, contingent / qualified-contingent and official open/close-print conditions; keep regular-way, ISO and odd-lot. Quotes: drop locked (bid = ask), crossed (bid > ask) and zero-price or zero-size quotes before any read. Historical trades are taken as delivered (corrections reflected by Alpaca); cancels are not modelled (recorded as a caveat).
amended: 2026-10-21, before any fetch, after result-skeptic FIX FIRST (5): a pre-step inventory of trade conditions and quote sizes per tape on 20 entries, with the keep/drop list registered as an amendment before any feature; locked / crossed / zero quotes dropped; 16,000 entries registered now, MDE projected outcome-blind from same-name control bar returns and judged at 5 bp; PRE population = all onsets (no IEX coverage rule); fetch plan with request budget, an after-hours window and resume across nights; a defined IEX live-feed bar; floors; within-hour and onset-bar-return information cells. Timing is shared with three_minute_reread (entry at the start of m).
amended_2: 2026-10-21 ~11:45 ET, before any tick is fetched, operator: 'there is no need to wait. If we need to stop the desk to run it, we can.' The after-hours fetch window (16:15-08:30 ET) is removed for every step. Ticks come from the data-only account (secrets_data.json), whose rate budget is separate from the desk's, and the bars-only steps run at nice 19; the pacing rule (<= 150 requests/min), the per-entry cache with resume, and the > 2% failure abort stay. If a fetch is ever seen to slow the live desk, it is stopped and resumed later (the operator has also allowed stopping the desk). No other rule changes; this touches no feature, outcome or verdict.
amended_3: 2026-10-21 ~12:05 ET, operator-approved ('yes'), before any feature or outcome is computed, from the pre-step inventory (ai_reports/order_flow_pilot/prestep.json: 20 entries, tapes A and C, 2,157 trades, 149 quotes, every trade with size and conditions, every quote with sizes, none locked/crossed/zero). (1) TRADE KEEP-LIST, exact: keep a trade only if EVERY one of its condition codes is in {' ' (CTA regular), '@' (UTP regular), 'I' (odd lot), 'F' (intermarket sweep)}; every other code drops the trade and is counted by code (observed: '4' derivatively priced, 'B' / 'W' average price, '7' qualified contingent, 'V' contingent; unseen codes such as extended-hours, out-of-sequence, prior-reference or official open/close prints drop the same way). (2) QUOTES are sparse (2 of 20 entries had no NBBO update in [T - 5 s, T + 1 s]; 10 had one), so: fetch NBBO quotes over [T - 120 s, T + 1 s] for the features; each trade is signed against the last quote at or before it, at most 60 s old, else the trade is UNSIGNED (counted, excluded from OFI60's numerator and denominator); an entry with fewer than 5 signed trades leaves G1 and G3 (the registered 'fewer than 5 trades' rule, now on signed trades). QI and MICRO use the last quote at or before T, at most 30 s old, else missing. (3) ENTRY / EXIT quotes: the last quote at or before the read time (T + 1 s, and T + 1 s + H), at most 30 s old, else the entry (or that horizon) is dropped and counted; outcome quote windows are [t - 30 s, t]. (4) Before the bulk fetch the 20-entry inventory is rerun with these windows to measure requests per entry; the fetch budget is re-stated from it.
